# PHASE 1 — RECONNECT
## Weeks 1–2

---

## Phase 1 Goals

Restore the neurological connection to the deep core and pelvic floor. Establish diaphragmatic breathing mechanics. Reduce post-surgical tension and stiffness. Build a sustainable daily movement habit. Begin progressive walking as the primary cardiovascular and functional activity.

---

## Phase 1 Nutrition Focus

Establish the eating pattern. Prioritise caloric adequacy — many women undereat in the early postpartum weeks. Target approximately 2,000–2,400 calories per day to support breastfeeding and healing. Protein at every meal. Hydration target of 2.5–3 litres daily. Evening snack to support overnight milk production. Begin postnatal multivitamin and vitamin D supplement if not already doing so.

Key foods this phase: Eggs, Greek yoghurt, oats, full-fat dairy, oily fish, lentils, avocado, bananas, nuts, and seeds. Batch cook where possible. Stock one-handed snack foods for feeding sessions.

---

## Phase 1 Supplements

- Postnatal multivitamin — daily
- Vitamin D — 10–25 micrograms daily
- Omega-3 DHA — 200–500mg daily
- Continue any supplements recommended by GP or midwife

---

## Week 1

### Daily Healing Session — 10–15 minutes, every day

**Opening — Diaphragmatic breathing**
10–15 breath cycles. Lying on back, knees bent. Lower hand rises, chest hand stays still. Inhale for 4 counts, exhale for 6. This is the foundation of everything that follows.

**Pelvic floor reconnection**
Gentle lift and release — 8–10 repetitions. Exhale to lift, inhale to release. The release is as important as the lift. If she feels nothing, this is normal. If she feels pain, stop.

Pelvic floor breathing — inhale to soften and descend, exhale to gently lift. Coordinate with diaphragm.

**Gentle mobility**
- Knee rolls supine — 8 per side. Slow, pain-free range only.
- Ankle circles — 10 each direction per foot.
- Foot pumps — 10 repetitions. Supports circulation post-surgery.

**Walking**
10 minutes daily. Flat terrain. RPE 3. Fully conversational pace. If pelvic heaviness or scar pain occurs, turn around immediately.

### Nutrition — Week 1 Priorities
Eat three meals and two to three snacks every day without exception. Do not skip meals. Prioritise protein at breakfast. Keep one-handed snacks within reach at all times. Drink water during every feeding session.

### Recovery — Week 1
Sleep whenever possible. Accept all offers of help with meals and household tasks. No lifting beyond the baby. Scar care as directed by surgical team.

---

## Week 2

### Daily Healing Session — 10–15 minutes, every day

**Diaphragmatic breathing** — as week 1, now adding awareness of ribcage expanding in all directions including into the back.

**Pelvic floor reconnection** — as week 1, now adding conscious awareness of full release after each lift. Begin to notice whether one side feels different from the other — note this for the pelvic floor physiotherapist.

**Gentle mobility**
- Knee rolls — 8 per side
- Ankle circles and foot pumps — as week 1
- Supported cat-cow on hands and knees — introduce if comfortable. Very small range of motion. Skip if hands and knees position is uncomfortable at the scar site.

**Walking**
Build from 10 minutes to 15–20 minutes across the week. Add 2–3 minutes every two days if symptom-free. Introduce very gentle inclines on days 5–7 if comfortable.

Walking progression:
- Days 1–2: 12 minutes
- Days 3–4: 15 minutes
- Days 5–7: 18–20 minutes

### Scar Care — Week 2
Begin desensitisation work. Using a soft cloth, gently touch the skin around — not on — the scar in different textures and pressures. 2–3 minutes daily. Many women find the area numb or hypersensitive. Both are normal.

### Phase 1 Check-In — End of Week 2

Before progressing to Phase 2, confirm all of the following.

- OB six-week clearance received
- 10 pelvic floor lifts performed with conscious control and full release
- No pain during or after daily sessions
- Walking 20 minutes comfortably at RPE 3–4
- Eating three meals and two to three snacks daily
- Pelvic floor physiotherapy appointment booked

If any criterion is not met, extend Phase 1 by one week and reassess.

---
---

# PHASE 2 — REBUILD FOUNDATION
## Weeks 3–6

---

## Phase 2 Goals

With OB clearance in place, begin activating the deep core system — specifically the transversus abdominis — in a controlled, pressure-managed way. Introduce scar tissue mobility work. Restore hip and thoracic mobility. Begin gentle lower body loading through bodyweight patterns progressing to resistance band loading. Build aerobic base through progressive walking and introduce alternative cardio modalities.

---

## Phase 2 Nutrition Focus

As activity increases, ensure caloric intake increases with it. Watch for signs of undereating — excessive fatigue, reduced milk supply, poor exercise recovery, mood deterioration. If any of these appear, the first question is always whether she is eating enough. Introduce batch cooking on weekends. Iron-rich foods twice to three times per week — red meat, lentils, dark leafy greens — to address post-surgical blood loss. Pair plant iron sources with vitamin C to enhance absorption. Post-exercise snack within 30–60 minutes of every session — protein plus carbohydrate.

---

## Phase 2 Scar Tissue Mobility Protocol

**Week 3 — Desensitisation**
Touch skin around the scar with soft cloth in different textures and pressures. 2–3 minutes daily. Not on the scar itself.

**Week 4 — Skin rolling above scar**
Gently pick up skin just above the scar line between thumb and forefinger and roll slowly. Mild pulling sensation is acceptable. Pain is not. 1–2 minutes daily.

**Week 6 — Direct scar massage**
Two fingers apply gentle downward pressure directly on the scar, moving in small circles — up, down, side to side. 2–3 minutes daily. If pulling into bladder or bowel is felt, refer to pelvic floor physiotherapist immediately.

---

## Week 3

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week, 20–30 minutes

**Session A — Posterior Chain and Core**
- Diaphragmatic breathing with TA connection — 3 sets of 8 breaths. Exhale to gently draw lower abdomen inward at 20–30% effort.
- Glute bridge — 3 × 10. Tempo 2-2-3-0. Exhale on rise.
- Heel slides — 3 × 8 per side. Slow and controlled. Neutral spine throughout.
- Four-point opposite arm and leg reach — 3 × 8 per side. 3-second hold at extension.
- Clamshell — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-1-3-0.

**Session B — Upper Body and Posture**
- Diaphragmatic breathing warm-up — 5 minutes
- Wall push-up — 3 × 10. Tempo 3-1-2-0. Straight body line throughout.
- Prone Y-T-W — 2 × 8 each shape. 2-second hold each position.
- Thoracic rotation side-lying — 2 × 8 per side. Breath-led movement.

**Session C — Full Body Bodyweight**
- Diaphragmatic breathing warm-up — 5 minutes
- Supported squat — 3 × 12. Tempo 3-1-2-0. Hold door frame or chair.
- Standing hip hinge — 3 × 10. Tempo 3-0-2-0. Spine long and neutral.
- Step-up onto bottom stair — 3 × 10 per side. Controlled throughout.
- Seated posture work — 5 minutes. Ribcage over pelvis, shoulder blades together and down.

### Cardio — Week 3
- Walking: 5–6 days, 20–25 minutes, RPE 4.
- Introduce pace variation from day 4: 2 minutes easy, 1 minute brisk, repeat × 5.
- Static cycling if available: Once per week, 15–20 minutes, RPE 4–5.

---

## Week 4

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**Progressions from week 3:**
- Glute bridge: Progress to 3-second hold at top. Introduce single-leg glute bridge if double-leg is symptom-free — 3 × 6 per side.
- Four-point reach: Increase hold to 5 seconds. Add 3-count controlled return.
- Wall push-up: Progress to incline push-up using sofa or low table.
- Supported squat: Remove support for final set only.
- Hip hinge: Add 3-second pause at bottom.

**All other exercises:** Repeat week 3 with focus on tempo quality and breathing consistency.

### Cardio — Week 4
- Walking: 5–6 days, 25–30 minutes, RPE 4–5.
- Interval progression: 2 minutes easy, 2 minutes brisk, repeat × 5.
- One longer walk: 35–40 minutes at RPE 4.
- Cycling if available: Once per week, 20 minutes, RPE 5.

---

## Week 5

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**New exercises introduced:**
- Sumo squat — 3 × 12. Feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out.
- Banded glute bridge — 3 × 12. Loop band above knees, press knees outward throughout.
- Banded clamshell — 3 × 15 per side. Slow eccentric.
- Banded hip abduction standing — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-2-3-0.
- Banded pull-apart — 3 × 12. Arms at shoulder height throughout.
- Banded seated row — 3 × 12. Band around feet, row to lower ribs.
- Banded squat — 3 × 12. Band above knees as knee tracking cue.

**Equipment introduced:** Light loop resistance band, light long resistance band.

### Cardio — Week 5
- Walking: 4–5 days, 30 minutes, RPE 4–5.
- Interval progression: 1 minute easy, 2 minutes brisk, repeat × 6.
- One longer walk: 40–45 minutes at RPE 4.
- Cycling: Once per week, 20–25 minutes with simple intervals — 3 minutes moderate, 1 minute higher resistance.
- Swimming: Introduce if scar fully healed and bleeding stopped — 20 minutes easy, RPE 4–5.

---

## Week 6

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**Progressions:**
- Banded glute bridge: Progress to single-leg banded glute bridge — 3 × 8 per side.
- Banded pull-apart: Increase to 15 reps or medium resistance band.
- Banded row: Increase to 15 reps.

**New exercises introduced:**
- Banded deadlift pattern — 3 × 10. Stand on long band, hip hinge with band resistance on return to standing. Tempo 3-1-2-0.
- Banded lateral walk — 2 × 12 steps each direction. Band above ankles.
- Banded glute kickback on all fours — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-2-3-0.

### Cardio — Week 6
- Walking: 4–5 days, 30–35 minutes, RPE 5.
- Power walking intervals: 1 minute easy, 3 minutes power walk at RPE 6, repeat × 5.
- One longer walk: 45–50 minutes at RPE 4–5.
- Cycling: Once per week, 25 minutes with intervals.
- Swimming: Once per week if cleared — 25 minutes, easy laps.

### Phase 2 Check-In — End of Week 6

Before progressing to Phase 3, confirm all of the following.

- Pelvic floor physiotherapist seen and report reviewed
- All Phase 2 exercises performed without doming, leaking, or pain
- Single-leg glute bridge — 8 reps per side with control
- Hip hinge under band resistance — consistent neutral spine
- Exhale-on-effort pattern automatic across all exercises
- Walking 30 minutes comfortably at RPE 5
- Eating post-exercise snack within 30–60 minutes consistently
- Scar desensitisation and skin rolling established as daily habit

If any criterion is not met, extend Phase 2 by one week in the relevant area and reassess.

# PHASE 3 — RESTORE FUNCTION
## Weeks 7–10

---

## Phase 3 Goals

Introduce dumbbell and kettlebell loading through established movement patterns. Build meaningful strength in the posterior chain, lower body, and upper body. Push cardiovascular intensity through structured interval training. Develop the physical capacity to manage the demands of daily life with a baby. Begin anti-movement core training and introduce oblique loading from week 10.

---

## Phase 3 Nutrition Focus

Post-exercise nutrition is now critical. Protein and carbohydrate within 30–60 minutes of every session. Review total protein intake — target 1.5–1.8g per kilogram of body weight daily. On higher intensity days — Sessions 1 and 3 — total caloric intake should be higher. Monitor milk supply as training intensity increases. If supply drops, increase caloric intake before reducing training volume. Hydration increases with training intensity — target 3 litres on training days.

---

8 minutes. Non-negotiable.

- Diaphragmatic breathing into core connection — 3–5 breath cycles lying down
- Hip circles standing — 10 each direction
- Leg swings front to back — 10 each leg
- Leg swings side to side — 10 each leg
- Thoracic rotation standing — 8 each side
- Arm circles — 10 each direction
- Banded glute bridge — 15 reps
- Banded clamshell — 10 per side
- Banded pull-apart — 12 reps
- Bodyweight squat — 8 reps, slow and deliberate
- Hip hinge — 8 reps
- Reverse lunge — 5 per side

# Full 12-Week Postpartum Return Programme
### Complete Summary Document
#### Client: 33-year-old, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, breastfeeding, home/yoga mat

---

## How to Use This Document

This summary consolidates every component of the programme into a single reference document. It is designed to be used alongside the detailed component guides already produced — the core restoration guide, the strength progression addendum, the nutrition plan, the cardio programming, and the HIIT reintroduction guide. Where this document says "as per strength guide" or "as per cardio protocol," refer to those detailed documents for full exercise descriptions, tempo prescriptions, and coaching cues.

This document gives you the complete picture — every week, every session, every component — in one place. Use it for session planning, client communication, and programme review.

---

## Standing Programme Rules — Apply Every Week

These rules govern every session of every phase without exception. Review them with your client at the start of the programme and revisit them at every phase transition.

**Rule 1 — Symptoms override programming.**
Any leaking, pelvic heaviness, scar pain, or midline doming means the exercise stops immediately. You are notified before the next session. The programme does not progress until the symptom is resolved and understood.

**Rule 2 — Exhale on effort.**
Every exercise, every rep, every set. The exhale coordinates the diaphragm and pelvic floor as a pressure management system. Breath holding is never acceptable.

**Rule 3 — Doming is a red line.**
If the midline rises into a ridge or cone during any exercise, that exercise is too demanding for the current state of the linea alba. Regress immediately.

**Rule 4 — Hunger means eat.**
She is breastfeeding and healing from surgery. Undereating compromises milk supply, delays healing, and impairs exercise recovery. Food is medicine at this stage.

**Rule 5 — Sleep deprivation affects everything.**
Sessions should leave her feeling better than when she started. If she arrives to a session severely sleep-deprived, reduce intensity. A depleted session does more harm than good.

**Rule 6 — Pelvic floor physiotherapy is non-negotiable.**
She should be seen by a pelvic floor physiotherapist at or just after her six-week OB check, and again before any direct abdominal loading is introduced. This is best practice, not optional.

**Rule 7 — Progress is earned, not assumed.**
Each progression — in load, volume, tempo, or exercise complexity — is earned by meeting the specific progression marker for the current level. If the marker is not met, the current level is repeated.

---

## Programme Overview at a Glance

| Phase | Weeks | Primary Focus | Sessions Per Week | Session Length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 — Reconnect | 1–2 | Breath, pelvic floor, walking | Daily 10–15 min healing sessions | 10–15 min |
| Phase 2 — Rebuild Foundation | 3–6 | Deep core, bodyweight to band loading, aerobic base | 3 strength + daily cardio | 20–30 min strength, 20–35 min cardio |
| Phase 3 — Restore Function | 7–10 | Dumbbell and kettlebell strength, structured cardio, intensity push | 4 strength + 3 cardio | 40–50 min strength, 35–45 min cardio |
| Phase 4 — Progress and Integrate | 11–12 | Compound loading, peak strength, low-impact HIIT preparation | 4 strength + 3 cardio | 45–50 min strength, 40–45 min cardio |

---
---

# PHASE 1 — RECONNECT
## Weeks 1–2

---

## Phase 1 Goals

Restore the neurological connection to the deep core and pelvic floor. Establish diaphragmatic breathing mechanics. Reduce post-surgical tension and stiffness. Build a sustainable daily movement habit. Begin progressive walking as the primary cardiovascular and functional activity.

---

## Phase 1 Nutrition Focus

Establish the eating pattern. Prioritise caloric adequacy — many women undereat in the early postpartum weeks. Target approximately 2,000–2,400 calories per day to support breastfeeding and healing. Protein at every meal. Hydration target of 2.5–3 litres daily. Evening snack to support overnight milk production. Begin postnatal multivitamin and vitamin D supplement if not already doing so.

Key foods this phase: Eggs, Greek yoghurt, oats, full-fat dairy, oily fish, lentils, avocado, bananas, nuts, and seeds. Batch cook where possible. Stock one-handed snack foods for feeding sessions.

---

## Phase 1 Supplements

- Postnatal multivitamin — daily
- Vitamin D — 10–25 micrograms daily
- Omega-3 DHA — 200–500mg daily
- Continue any supplements recommended by GP or midwife

---

## Week 1

### Daily Healing Session — 10–15 minutes, every day

**Opening — Diaphragmatic breathing**
10–15 breath cycles. Lying on back, knees bent. Lower hand rises, chest hand stays still. Inhale for 4 counts, exhale for 6. This is the foundation of everything that follows.

**Pelvic floor reconnection**
Gentle lift and release — 8–10 repetitions. Exhale to lift, inhale to release. The release is as important as the lift. If she feels nothing, this is normal. If she feels pain, stop.

Pelvic floor breathing — inhale to soften and descend, exhale to gently lift. Coordinate with diaphragm.

**Gentle mobility**
- Knee rolls supine — 8 per side. Slow, pain-free range only.
- Ankle circles — 10 each direction per foot.
- Foot pumps — 10 repetitions. Supports circulation post-surgery.

**Walking**
10 minutes daily. Flat terrain. RPE 3. Fully conversational pace. If pelvic heaviness or scar pain occurs, turn around immediately.

### Nutrition — Week 1 Priorities
Eat three meals and two to three snacks every day without exception. Do not skip meals. Prioritise protein at breakfast. Keep one-handed snacks within reach at all times. Drink water during every feeding session.

### Recovery — Week 1
Sleep whenever possible. Accept all offers of help with meals and household tasks. No lifting beyond the baby. Scar care as directed by surgical team.

---

## Week 2

### Daily Healing Session — 10–15 minutes, every day

**Diaphragmatic breathing** — as week 1, now adding awareness of ribcage expanding in all directions including into the back.

**Pelvic floor reconnection** — as week 1, now adding conscious awareness of full release after each lift. Begin to notice whether one side feels different from the other — note this for the pelvic floor physiotherapist.

**Gentle mobility**
- Knee rolls — 8 per side
- Ankle circles and foot pumps — as week 1
- Supported cat-cow on hands and knees — introduce if comfortable. Very small range of motion. Skip if hands and knees position is uncomfortable at the scar site.

**Walking**
Build from 10 minutes to 15–20 minutes across the week. Add 2–3 minutes every two days if symptom-free. Introduce very gentle inclines on days 5–7 if comfortable.

Walking progression:
- Days 1–2: 12 minutes
- Days 3–4: 15 minutes
- Days 5–7: 18–20 minutes

### Scar Care — Week 2
Begin desensitisation work. Using a soft cloth, gently touch the skin around — not on — the scar in different textures and pressures. 2–3 minutes daily. Many women find the area numb or hypersensitive. Both are normal.

### Phase 1 Check-In — End of Week 2

Before progressing to Phase 2, confirm all of the following.

- OB six-week clearance received
- 10 pelvic floor lifts performed with conscious control and full release
- No pain during or after daily sessions
- Walking 20 minutes comfortably at RPE 3–4
- Eating three meals and two to three snacks daily
- Pelvic floor physiotherapy appointment booked

If any criterion is not met, extend Phase 1 by one week and reassess.

---
---

# PHASE 2 — REBUILD FOUNDATION
## Weeks 3–6

---

## Phase 2 Goals

With OB clearance in place, begin activating the deep core system — specifically the transversus abdominis — in a controlled, pressure-managed way. Introduce scar tissue mobility work. Restore hip and thoracic mobility. Begin gentle lower body loading through bodyweight patterns progressing to resistance band loading. Build aerobic base through progressive walking and introduce alternative cardio modalities.

---

## Phase 2 Nutrition Focus

As activity increases, ensure caloric intake increases with it. Watch for signs of undereating — excessive fatigue, reduced milk supply, poor exercise recovery, mood deterioration. If any of these appear, the first question is always whether she is eating enough. Introduce batch cooking on weekends. Iron-rich foods twice to three times per week — red meat, lentils, dark leafy greens — to address post-surgical blood loss. Pair plant iron sources with vitamin C to enhance absorption. Post-exercise snack within 30–60 minutes of every session — protein plus carbohydrate.

---

## Phase 2 Scar Tissue Mobility Protocol

**Week 3 — Desensitisation**
Touch skin around the scar with soft cloth in different textures and pressures. 2–3 minutes daily. Not on the scar itself.

**Week 4 — Skin rolling above scar**
Gently pick up skin just above the scar line between thumb and forefinger and roll slowly. Mild pulling sensation is acceptable. Pain is not. 1–2 minutes daily.

**Week 6 — Direct scar massage**
Two fingers apply gentle downward pressure directly on the scar, moving in small circles — up, down, side to side. 2–3 minutes daily. If pulling into bladder or bowel is felt, refer to pelvic floor physiotherapist immediately.

---

## Week 3

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week, 20–30 minutes

**Session A — Posterior Chain and Core**
- Diaphragmatic breathing with TA connection — 3 sets of 8 breaths. Exhale to gently draw lower abdomen inward at 20–30% effort.
- Glute bridge — 3 × 10. Tempo 2-2-3-0. Exhale on rise.
- Heel slides — 3 × 8 per side. Slow and controlled. Neutral spine throughout.
- Four-point opposite arm and leg reach — 3 × 8 per side. 3-second hold at extension.
- Clamshell — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-1-3-0.

**Session B — Upper Body and Posture**
- Diaphragmatic breathing warm-up — 5 minutes
- Wall push-up — 3 × 10. Tempo 3-1-2-0. Straight body line throughout.
- Prone Y-T-W — 2 × 8 each shape. 2-second hold each position.
- Thoracic rotation side-lying — 2 × 8 per side. Breath-led movement.

**Session C — Full Body Bodyweight**
- Diaphragmatic breathing warm-up — 5 minutes
- Supported squat — 3 × 12. Tempo 3-1-2-0. Hold door frame or chair.
- Standing hip hinge — 3 × 10. Tempo 3-0-2-0. Spine long and neutral.
- Step-up onto bottom stair — 3 × 10 per side. Controlled throughout.
- Seated posture work — 5 minutes. Ribcage over pelvis, shoulder blades together and down.

### Cardio — Week 3
- Walking: 5–6 days, 20–25 minutes, RPE 4.
- Introduce pace variation from day 4: 2 minutes easy, 1 minute brisk, repeat × 5.
- Static cycling if available: Once per week, 15–20 minutes, RPE 4–5.

---

## Week 4

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**Progressions from week 3:**
- Glute bridge: Progress to 3-second hold at top. Introduce single-leg glute bridge if double-leg is symptom-free — 3 × 6 per side.
- Four-point reach: Increase hold to 5 seconds. Add 3-count controlled return.
- Wall push-up: Progress to incline push-up using sofa or low table.
- Supported squat: Remove support for final set only.
- Hip hinge: Add 3-second pause at bottom.

**All other exercises:** Repeat week 3 with focus on tempo quality and breathing consistency.

### Cardio — Week 4
- Walking: 5–6 days, 25–30 minutes, RPE 4–5.
- Interval progression: 2 minutes easy, 2 minutes brisk, repeat × 5.
- One longer walk: 35–40 minutes at RPE 4.
- Cycling if available: Once per week, 20 minutes, RPE 5.

---

## Week 5

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**New exercises introduced:**
- Sumo squat — 3 × 12. Feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out.
- Banded glute bridge — 3 × 12. Loop band above knees, press knees outward throughout.
- Banded clamshell — 3 × 15 per side. Slow eccentric.
- Banded hip abduction standing — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-2-3-0.
- Banded pull-apart — 3 × 12. Arms at shoulder height throughout.
- Banded seated row — 3 × 12. Band around feet, row to lower ribs.
- Banded squat — 3 × 12. Band above knees as knee tracking cue.

**Equipment introduced:** Light loop resistance band, light long resistance band.

### Cardio — Week 5
- Walking: 4–5 days, 30 minutes, RPE 4–5.
- Interval progression: 1 minute easy, 2 minutes brisk, repeat × 6.
- One longer walk: 40–45 minutes at RPE 4.
- Cycling: Once per week, 20–25 minutes with simple intervals — 3 minutes moderate, 1 minute higher resistance.
- Swimming: Introduce if scar fully healed and bleeding stopped — 20 minutes easy, RPE 4–5.

---

## Week 6

### Strength Sessions — 3 per week

**Progressions:**
- Banded glute bridge: Progress to single-leg banded glute bridge — 3 × 8 per side.
- Banded pull-apart: Increase to 15 reps or medium resistance band.
- Banded row: Increase to 15 reps.

**New exercises introduced:**
- Banded deadlift pattern — 3 × 10. Stand on long band, hip hinge with band resistance on return to standing. Tempo 3-1-2-0.
- Banded lateral walk — 2 × 12 steps each direction. Band above ankles.
- Banded glute kickback on all fours — 3 × 12 per side. Tempo 2-2-3-0.

### Cardio — Week 6
- Walking: 4–5 days, 30–35 minutes, RPE 5.
- Power walking intervals: 1 minute easy, 3 minutes power walk at RPE 6, repeat × 5.
- One longer walk: 45–50 minutes at RPE 4–5.
- Cycling: Once per week, 25 minutes with intervals.
- Swimming: Once per week if cleared — 25 minutes, easy laps.

### Phase 2 Check-In — End of Week 6

Before progressing to Phase 3, confirm all of the following.

- Pelvic floor physiotherapist seen and report reviewed
- All Phase 2 exercises performed without doming, leaking, or pain
- Single-leg glute bridge — 8 reps per side with control
- Hip hinge under band resistance — consistent neutral spine
- Exhale-on-effort pattern automatic across all exercises
- Walking 30 minutes comfortably at RPE 5
- Eating post-exercise snack within 30–60 minutes consistently
- Scar desensitisation and skin rolling established as daily habit

If any criterion is not met, extend Phase 2 by one week in the relevant area and reassess.

---
---

# PHASE 3 — RESTORE FUNCTION
## Weeks 7–10

---

## Phase 3 Goals

Introduce dumbbell and kettlebell loading through established movement patterns. Build meaningful strength in the posterior chain, lower body, and upper body. Push cardiovascular intensity through structured interval training. Develop the physical capacity to manage the demands of daily life with a baby. Begin anti-movement core training and introduce oblique loading from week 10.

---

## Phase 3 Nutrition Focus

Post-exercise nutrition is now critical. Protein and carbohydrate within 30–60 minutes of every session. Review total protein intake — target 1.5–1.8g per kilogram of body weight daily. On higher intensity days — Sessions 1 and 3 — total caloric intake should be higher. Monitor milk supply as training intensity increases. If supply drops, increase caloric intake before reducing training volume. Hydration increases with training intensity — target 3 litres on training days.

---

## Phase 3 Warm-Up Protocol — Every Session

8 minutes. Non-negotiable.

- Diaphragmatic breathing into core connection — 3–5 breath cycles lying down
- Hip circles standing — 10 each direction
- Leg swings front to back — 10 each leg
- Leg swings side to side — 10 each leg
- Thoracic rotation standing — 8 each side
- Arm circles — 10 each direction
- Banded glute bridge — 15 reps
- Banded clamshell — 10 per side
- Banded pull-apart — 12 reps
- Bodyweight squat — 8 reps, slow and deliberate
- Hip hinge — 8 reps
- Reverse lunge — 5 per side

---

## Phase 3 Weekly Structure

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Monday | Lower Body Strength |
| Tuesday | Cardio Session A — Intervals |
| Wednesday | Upper Body and Core |
| Thursday | Cardio Session B — Steady State |
| Friday | Full Body Power Endurance |
| Saturday | Cardio Session C — Long Easy Walk |
| Sunday | Rest |

---

## Week 7

### Equipment Introduced
Dumbbells: 2kg, 3kg, 4kg, 5kg, 6kg. Resistance bands continuing from Phase 2.

### Session 1 — Lower Body Strength (Monday)

Superset A — 4 rounds, 75 seconds rest between supersets:
- A1. Goblet squat — 4 × 8 @ 6kg. Tempo 4-1-2-0.
- A2. Banded glute bridge with dumbbell — 4 × 12 @ 8–10kg across hips. Tempo 2-2-2-2.

Superset B — 4 rounds, 75 seconds rest:
- B1. Romanian deadlift — 4 × 10 @ 4kg each hand. Tempo 4-1-2-0.
- B2. Reverse lunge — 4 × 10 per side @ 4kg each hand. Tempo 3-1-2-0.

Straight sets:
- C. Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 10 per side. Tempo 2-3-2-0. Bodyweight.
- D. Pallof press — 3 × 10 per side. Tempo 2-3-2-0.

### Session 2 — Upper Body and Core (Wednesday)

Superset A — 4 rounds:
- A1. Dumbbell floor press — 4 × 10 @ 5–6kg each hand. Tempo 4-1-2-1.
- A2. Dumbbell bent-over row — 4 × 10 per side @ 6–8kg. Tempo 2-2-3-0.

Superset B — 4 rounds:
- B1. Dumbbell overhead press — 4 × 8 @ 4–5kg each hand. Tempo 3-1-2-1.
- B2. Prone Y-T-W with dumbbells — 3 × 8 each shape @ 1–2kg. Tempo 2-3-2-0.

Superset C — 3 rounds:
- C1. Side plank from knees — 3 × 30–40 seconds per side.
- C2. Dead bug — 3 × 8 per side. Tempo 3-3-3-0.

Finisher — 3 rounds minimal rest:
- Banded pull-apart × 15
- Dumbbell lateral raise × 12 @ 2kg
- Dumbbell bicep curl × 12 @ 4kg

Block 1 — EMOM 10 minutes:
- Odd minutes: Goblet squat × 8 @ 6kg
- Even minutes: Dumbbell bent-over row × 8 per side @ 6kg

Block 2 — Circuit, 3 rounds, 45 seconds work, 15 seconds transition, 90 seconds rest between rounds:
- Reverse lunge alternating @ 4kg each hand
- Dumbbell floor press @ 5kg each hand
- Romanian deadlift @ 8kg each hand
- Banded lateral walk — 10 steps each direction

- Dumbbell overhead press @ 4kg each hand

Block 3 — Finisher, 2 rounds:
- Banded glute bridge × 20
- Pallof press × 10 per side
- Side plank hold × 30 seconds per side

- Sumo Romanian deadlift — 3 × 12 @ 8kg single dumbbell
- Superset: Banded clamshell × 20 per side + Banded hip abduction standing × 15 per side — 3 rounds

### Cardio — Week 7
